_: youtube/default SFX map. WHAT only: event -> sound class -> library file + slice. Numbers measured off the your-job intro. Read by workflows/sfx-plan.py; placement is per lane (LANES.md step 6).

targets_dbfs._: on-timeline PEAK per class; the clip level is target minus the measured slice peak, whole dB, capped at +6; an event carrying level_db uses that fixed clip level instead; the voice ceiling these bands sit under is the -6 dBFS limiter of step 3

tracks._: LAYER ROLES, not a fixed layout: primary / layer2 / layer3 / music. The values are the 0-based audio track indices of the Premiere/Resolve map in this preset's README (A2/A3/A4/A5); a lane whose audio tracks are laid out differently maps by ROLE and ignores the numbers

_density: 2026-09-10: a slam/Impact owns ±stamp_owns_beat_s of its own graphic (the scissors around it, the stroke under it, a pop are dropped; the cut-in, the scene changes (slideIn/slideOut), beds and hand entries stay); across all graphics never more than max_per_second sounds in a rolling second (lowest priority goes: marker < word < rise/slide < pop < slam < cut-in < Impact/character; beds not counted; hand entries never dropped). sfx.md § Density.

slam._: Metal Pop, your slice (2026-09-03): the transient sits a frame in, tail trimmed

reveal._: text typing on: real typing at a real level, not a texture (2026-09-03: +2 dB on the .aiff)

flash._: PAIRED with the flicker/flash animation (2026-09-03: 'those are paired'): one Neon Flicker at the strobe START, whole file, fixed 0 dB clip level. No stamp on the landing. A full-screen that opens on a flicker takes this INSTEAD of the cut-in whoosh.

word._: you 2026-09-03: scissor snips at a FIXED -7 dB clip level (was -3, then -5) on every RISE text-animation word (level_db overrides the class target). Texting On Phone is kept in reserve for a stepping/ticking event.

cut-in._: a hard cut INTO a full-screen, 2 frames early. DROPPED when a flash/flicker sits within 2 frames of the cut (the flicker sound is the cut's sound then).

word-pop._: RETIRED 2026-09-10 (you: type never pops; animations.md § TEXT NEVER POPS). Kept so an old job's plan still resolves; the builder refuses the entrance now. a text animation whose ENTRANCE is punch/pop: each word gets the object pop

word-slam._: a SLAM text animation: Impact on every word, 2 frames after the word onset (on the settle), fixed -10 dB; the run truncates itself and the last word rings out (your 'one shot', 2026-09-03)

events._slices: a single-hit whoosh file (Simple Whoosh 1/2, Whoosh Short 2) is placed WHOLE; every other library file is multi-hit or long and is always sliced (2026-09-03)

word-flicker._: a text animation with the flicker entrance strobes as ONE block: one Neon Flicker at the block's first word onset, nothing per word

word-negative._: NEGATION (2026-09-03): a RED word in a text animation is a negative beat and takes the Error Buzz instead of scissors, fixed -7 dB (his 'defeats' placement). The same sound is the candidate for an X or a strike-through; not automatic there yet.

emphasis._: Named in the comp (data-sfx=\"emphasis\" on the element) or in a hand row; the planner never guesses it. 2026-09-10: use these freely. a SCRIPT call, never automatic (2026-09-03): an especially important word gets an Impact 2 frames after its onset and loses its scissors. Named in sfx-hand.json as {gid, event: emphasis, word}. Styling alone (serif/italic) does NOT trigger it.

gunshot._: Named in the comp (data-sfx=\"gunshot\" on the element) or in a hand row; the planner never guesses it. 2026-09-10: use these freely. a literal prop: bullet holes, a shot. Hand entry; drops the pop it replaces. Fixed -15 dB (the file peaks at 0 dBFS). Leads by 2 frames: the mp3's attack sits ~70 ms into the file, so the bang lands ON the hole (you placed hole 1 two frames early).

row-tick._: a list row / rule ticking on: a switch click, not an object pop. Automatic: a pop inside a list/card-kind graphic becomes this (your rules card, 2026-09-03).

payoff._: AUTOMATIC since 2026-09-10 (you: 'in special scenarios where it's green or showing completion or goodness, it's nice to represent that with sound'): sfx-plan.py reads the completion signal off the markup (a completion class such as hi/done/check, completion words in the element's own text, a green fill/stroke on or inside it, a green CSS rule it satisfies, or data-sfx="payoff"; data-sfx="pop" opts out) and rings the bell instead of the pop/slam/row-tick it replaces. A hand entry still works. Earned on your-job's 'Postable Edit' node (green, the finished state), which popped. a completion / reward beat (100%, the finished node, a check): Bell Ding starting 4 frames BEFORE the visual lands so the attack rings with it. drops the pop it replaces.

processing._: Named in the comp (data-sfx=\"processing\" on the element) or in a hand row; the planner never guesses it. 2026-09-10: use these freely. software WORKING: the bed under a scrub / render / think span in a scene that depicts an app. Hand entry with dur. (No longer the count-up sound.)

click._: Named in the comp (data-sfx=\"click\" on the element) or in a hand row; the planner never guesses it. 2026-09-10: use these freely. a cursor ACTION inside a scene that depicts software (the cursor arrives on its target, a razor lands). Hand entry per action.

rec._: a RECORDING STARTS: the REC badge / timecode of a camera UI enacting a recording (g24, your-job). The tonal onset of the beep-and-shutter file, picked by spectral flatness; heard and approved by you 2026-09-10 ('that was good, you can keep that one'). Named in the comp with data-sfx="rec" on the badge (it replaces the badge's pop).

camera._: a CAMERA prop or a camera UI LANDING (viewfinder brackets, a shutter frame): the click of the thing itself, replacing the prop's pop. your own pick over Analogue Camera Snap, placed by hand at a fixed -2 dB and approved by ear (your-job g11, 2026-09-19). Named in the comp with data-sfx="camera", or in a hand row.

hand_entries: hf-graphics/sfx-hand.json rows: {gid, event, at (comp seconds) | word (a span in a text comp), dur?, note?, level_db? (override), drop? ([events] to remove from that comp's automatic list, e.g. the pops a gunshot/payoff replaces)}
_judgement: 2026-09-10: the palette is the DOCUMENTED map and only that (an undocumented library file cannot be heard by the planner or its author: the chat-bubble blips were 'heinous'). The freedom is where a documented sound goes: data-sfx="<event>" on the element names any event in this file, data-sfx="none" silences one, a hand row does the same for an unbindable timing; data-sfx-file and a hand row's `file` are refused. New sounds enter here after you have listened.
